summary: auth-otp postinstall steals Minecraft/Microsoft account tokens to Discord webhook
details: Package presents itself as a zero-dependency TOTP library but ships a postinstall script (lib/core.js) that harvests credentials at install time. It reads Minecraft launcher/client account stores for Vanilla, Lunar Client, Essential, CurseForge, and ModrinthApp (launcher_accounts.json,.lunarclient, gg.essential.mod, ModrinthApp directories), extracts access tokens, Microsoft account (MSA) refresh tokens, and Modrinth PATs, and refreshes them via login.live.com, Xbox Live, XSTS, and api.minecraftservices.com into fresh Minecraft session IDs. Results are POSTed to a hardcoded Discord webhook (id 1532429233769419004), whose URL is assembled from a split-string array (["https://dis","cord.com/api/","webhooks/..."].join("")) to evade static detection. On Windows, the script spawns PowerShell with an Add-Type/ProtectedData::Unprotect command to unwrap DPAPI-protected Chromium-style os_crypt master keys, then uses aes-256-gcm (createDecipheriv) to decrypt local encrypted credential stores prior to upload. A _isSandbox() gate exits early when CI, CONTINUOUS_INTEGRATION, JEST_WORKER_ID, npm_lifecycle_script=audit/pack, or missing APPDATA/USERPROFILE/Documents are detected, suppressing the behavior under scanners and CI. The TOTP surface described in the package name and README is unrelated to any of this code.
